nodes.text: Northern relay operator Pavel Rezek requesting inter-regional transfer. Authorization code N-301.

answers.reply: Station failure.
South sector communications office. Supposedly.
You already checked the code, did you not?

nodes.text: The official report says electrical fire.

answers.reply: The station stopped being useful to them.
Most of us.
You should avoid reading too deeply into reports.

nodes.text: You know how transfers work. Different building. Same voice on the radio.

answers.text: Ask how long he worked there
answers.reply: Long enough.

answers.text: Ask if he liked the job
answers.reply: At first.
I imagine your station looks very similar to mine.

nodes.text: Operators are valuable right until they start thinking independently.

answers.reply: You already know what I mean.
Everyone does eventually.
Do not sound so nervous, {PLAYER_NAME}.

nodes.text: A few disappeared after the investigation.

answers.reply: Unauthorized transmissions. Delayed denials. Missing reports.
You should always file your reports on time.

nodes.text: Long enough to memorize the sound of people lying over weak signals.

answers.text: Ask if he can tell when you lie
answers.reply: Usually.
You hesitate before difficult choices too, don't you?

nodes.text: You feel important during the first weeks. Then the voices start staying with you.

answers.reply: The ones you denied. Mostly the quiet ones.
That part comes later.

nodes.text: They sent you the child too, didn't they?

answers.text: Ask how he knows about the child
answers.reply: Because they sent one to me.
Thought so.
The tests become more obvious after a while.

nodes.text: First you bend protocol for someone desperate. Then you start wondering why the protocol exists at all.

answers.text: Ask if he helped people cross
answers.reply: Sometimes.
The system notices patterns eventually.

nodes.text: Funny thing is, they already knew which operators were guilty before questioning started.

answers.reply: Decision timing. Voice stress. Frequency of manual overrides.
You should assume every delay is recorded.

nodes.text: You are wondering whether I am warning you or testing you.

answers.reply: Does it matter?
Paranoia becomes part of the routine.

nodes.text: You start hearing them after shifts. Even when the radio is off.

answers.reply: Do not worry. That part comes later.

nodes.text: Young voice. No valid ID. Said someone was waiting beyond the border.

answers.reply: What do you think I did?
You sound exactly like I did.

nodes.text: Silence usually means guilt. Or fear. Sometimes both.

answers.reply: You should be careful which one they see in you.

nodes.text: Then one night I realized I stopped asking who deserved help.

answers.reply: I still do not know.
Maybe that was the moment they marked my file.

nodes.text: Operators think they monitor the border. Really, the border monitors them.

answers.reply: You should remember that.

nodes.text: You will still think about this conversation after your shift ends.

answers.reply: That is enough for me.

nodes.text: The difficult part is not opening the gate. It is remembering the ones you kept closed.

answers.reply: That stays with you longer.

nodes.text: Systems survive by convincing people that mercy is dangerous.

answers.reply: Eventually you stop knowing whether they were right.

nodes.text: My transfer authorization is valid. But then again, so was yours when you arrived.

answers.reply: Take care of the station, operator.
Yeah. I expected that.
